title: JPMorgan, Stanley Race To Block AI Agents Accessing Customer Accounts Without Instructions
description: The prominent banks in America detected multiple third-party AI agents with key credentials of the users but they acted beyond their instructions The report suggested that these unauthorized AI agents were operating inside customer accounts adding that some even attempted to take actions that appeared to be independent of user interactions

title: Panel discussion on AI, innovation, entrepreneurship held at KU
description: Srinagar, Oct 23: The University of Kashmir (KU) on Friday hosted a panel discussion on “Future Forward: AI, Innovation and Entrepreneurship” at the Main Campus bringing students, scholars and faculty members together to discuss the opportunities and challenges shaping the future of technology. Held in collaboration with Intel India, the programme featured a fireside chat and a panel discussion with Gokul V. Subramaniam, President, Intel India, Vice President, Client Computing Group, and General Manager, Client Computing Platforms and Systems, Intel Corporation. The event aimed to promote direct dialogue between academia and industry, familiarise students with developments in artificial intelligence, and encourage an innovation and entrepreneurial mindset. It also sought to inspire students to pursue research, start-ups and technology careers. In her keynote address, Vice-Chancellor KU Prof. Nilofer Khan highlighted the significance of AI in education and research. She said that engagement with industry can help bridge the gap between classroom learning and industry needs, particularly in a region facing geographical challenges. During the panel discussion, Prof. Khan spoke about the University’s efforts to integrate AI into academics, research, innovation, entrepreneurship, start-ups, administration and governance. She also referred to work in data science and robotics and stressed the need to keep students and scholars abreast of technological change through skill development and capacity-building. During his interaction Gokul V. Subramaniam advised students to keep learning and remain curious as technology changes rapidly. He emphasised the importance of strengthening the fundamentals of their disciplines, asking questions and developing the ability to adapt. He also spoke about AI’s potential to personalise learning and encouraged participants to use the technology ethically. He said that aspiration, ability and attitude are among the qualities industry looks for in prospective human resources. Earlier in his welcome address, Registrar KU Prof. Naseer Iqbal referred to the Memorandum of Understanding signed between the University and Intel India in May 2024 under Intel’s AI for Future Workforce programme. He said AI is reshaping industry, academics, research and everyday life and called on universities to help students become problem-solvers and leaders in technological development. Dr. Manzoor Ahmad Chachoo moderated the panel discussion while as Prof. Aijaz A. Wani proposed the vote of thanks on the occasion. Dr. Javed Ahmad Sheikh, coordinated the event and also conducted the proceedings.

title: SpaceX’s $40 billion AI debt plan faces market turmoil. Can investors stomach the growing borrowing risks?
description: SpaceX’s efforts to finalize a $40 billion off-balance-sheet debt structure for its artificial intelligence buildout have been roiled by recent market turmoil that’s driven up sector-wide borrowing costs and complicated price talks.

title: UK pledges £600m to defend against AI health and security threats
description: The UK has pledged to spend £600m to defend the public against threats to health and security from artificial intelligence.
